facts.text: Time to collision is the seconds remaining before two objects meet if nothing changes; time headway is the seconds a machine needs to reach an object's current position; trigger distance is the range at which the system must act.
facts.quote: Time to collision is how many seconds remain before two things meet if nothing changes, time headway is how many seconds the machine needs to reach the spot an object occupies now, and trigger distance is the range at which the system must act.

facts.text: Time to collision is the most common quantity in road-car automatic braking, where a 1.0 s trigger was used as a research convention.
facts.quote: It is the most common quantity in road-car automatic braking, where a 1.0 s trigger was used as a research convention

facts.text: Road-car automatic braking systems stage warning, partial braking and full braking at falling time-to-collision values.
facts.quote: systems stage warning, partial and full braking at falling TTC values [Chapter 8]

facts.text: The booklet encounters time headway only as a distance in on-road test setups, with 12 to 40 m between vehicles.
facts.quote: The booklet meets headway only as a distance in on-road test setups, 12 to 40 m between vehicles

facts.text: The nearest off-road relative of the booklet's on-road headway test distances is a 50 m following distance in a Chinese underground regulation.
facts.quote: its nearest off-road relative is a 50 m following distance in a Chinese underground regulation [Chapter 3]

facts.text: The booklet expresses trigger distance as D_trigger = D_detect + v x T_action + D_stop + D_safety: detection and confirmation distance, distance traveled while the command takes effect, physical stopping distance, and safety clearance. This follows the ISO 21815-3 structure.
facts.quote: `D_trigger = D_detect + v x T_action + D_stop + D_safety`: the distance spent detecting and confirming, the distance traveled while the command takes effect, the physical stopping distance, and a safety clearance, which is the ISO 21815-3 structure [Chapter 8]

facts.text: An early haul-truck study derived detection ranges of 15 m to the sides, 50 m to the rear and 100 m to the front from a 0.5 s reaction time plus braking.
facts.quote: an early haul-truck study derived detection ranges of 15 m to the sides, 50 m to the rear and 100 m to the front from a 0.5 s reaction time plus braking

facts.text: A mining-truck patent uses two time-to-collision limits with 1 to 3 s added for operator reaction.
facts.quote: a mining-truck patent uses two TTC limits with 1 to 3 s added for operator reaction [Chapter 8]

facts.text: The booklet rates a fixed time-to-collision threshold as a weak primary trigger at work-site speeds and favors a distance-and-zone formulation, retaining TTC for faster haul traffic and as a diagnostic input.
facts.quote: The booklet rates a fixed TTC threshold "a weak primary trigger at work-site speeds" and favors the distance-and-zone formulation, with TTC retained for faster haul traffic and as a diagnostic input [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Assumed reaction times in the booklet's sources range from 0.5 s to 2.5 s, so the same time-to-collision rule can imply very different trigger distances.
facts.quote: Assumed reaction times in the sources range from 0.5 s to 2.5 s, so the same TTC rule can mean very different trigger distances [Chapter 8].
